newsitem.title: USA: ConAgra Q3 refrigerated foods profit up.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra Q3 refrigerated foods profit up.

text.p: ConAgra Inc said Thursday its refrigerated foods segment posted a 35 percent rise in operating profit in the third quarter ended February 23, while profits dropped 11 percent in the first nine months, compared with year-ago periods.

Segment sales were off two percent in the third quarter and decreased three percent in the nine months, primarily due to beef and poultry restructuring initiatives that were taken after the year-ago third quarter.
ConAgra did not release specific segment earnings. Overall income rose to $0.63 a share in the quarter from $0.55.

Branded processed meats, the segments' largest profit contributor, posted double-digit operating profit growth in the third quarter and the first nine months of 1997. U.S. beef operating profit rebounded sharply in the third quarter and was up for the first nine months.
ConAgra said its Australian beef operating profit improved substantially in the quarter and nine months.

Third quarter pork profits dropped in the third quarter and nine months. ConAgra said the earnings were "satisfactory" in light of high raw material costs in the industry. Poultry profit decreased and cheese profits were down in both periods.
ConAgra said its grocery/diversified products segment reported a 12 percent rise in operating profit in the third quarter, and posted a 20 percent gain in the nine months.
Segment sales rose four percent in the quarter and eight percent through the nine months.
ConAgra said its frozen foods posted more than a 20 percent operating profit in the third quarter and nine months.

Combined Hunt-Wesson/Frozen Foods unit volumes were down about three percent in the third quarter, reflecting sluggish categories and soft grocery industry sales, ConAgra said. For the nine months, unit volumes were up nearly four percent.

ConAgra's food inputs and ingredients segment had a 14 percent drop in operating profit in the third quarter, but a six percent increase in the first nine months. Segment sales fell 10 percent in the quarter and one percent for the nine months. Business dispositions, lower wheat prices and reduced international fertilizer sales drove the decline, it said.

Third quarter operating profit gains in a number of businesses, particularly flour milling and specialty food ingredients, were more than offset by declines in other businesses, especially specialty grain and grain merchandising.
